input.task: What is the title on this page?

provenance: found on 2026-08-18, when openlibrary.org came back from its outage and `live-ol-edition-title` kept failing `nav` anyway. The outage had been masking a real limitation: an eval-side probe loaded the same URL in **4.4s** under `wait_until="domcontentloaded"`, with the expected heading 'The monk and the dancer' already in the accessibility tree, and timed out at **25s** under `wait_until="load"` — Playwright's default, and what `run_task`'s `page.goto` relied on. One hanging subresource made a page whose every word was available unreadable to the agent.

triage.direction: a FALSE failure, the safe direction — the same family as evidence-window-keeps-the-anchor. It never invents an answer; it refuses to read a page it can see. The cost is a `failure:nav` that blames the site for the agent's own wait condition, and a support-matrix row that would have recorded a live domain as unreachable when it was merely slow to finish decorating itself.
triage.watched_red: before the fix: failure:nav, 'Page.goto: Timeout 20000ms exceeded', after burning the full 20s budget. After: success in well under a second — `domcontentloaded` fires immediately and the image goes on hanging in the background, unwatched and unneeded.
triage.why_domcontentloaded_is_not_a_downgrade: DOMContentLoaded fires after the HTML is parsed and deferred/inline scripts have run — everything a JS-rendered page puts in the DOM synchronously is already there. What `load` adds is images, stylesheets and subframes, which no locator tier reads. Content that genuinely arrives later was never guaranteed by `load` either, and is covered by check_state's settle loop (SETTLE_TRIES × SETTLE_MS) and by the `render-delayed` mutation.
triage.fixture_note: /fixtures/hang.png sleeps 120s and is never awaited to completion; the eval closes the browser first. The 20s cost of this case is paid once, while watching it red — green, it is one of the fastest cases in the suite.
